reproduction_target: Lift&Add, a Snakemake+bash workflow that maps vertebrate conserved elements from a reference genome (mouse mm10) onto new genome assemblies with UCSC liftOver and Liftoff, then adds the newly lifted sequences back into the per-element multiple-species alignments with MAFFT --add. The paper is hybrid: it both ships the pipeline (code/Lift_and_Add in the authors' GitLab repository) and runs an application analysis whose biological conclusions matter. Computational target as demonstrated: (1) a re-analysis of thylacine/wolf lineage-specific acceleration on a 61-way vertebrate whole-genome alignment obtained privately from Charlie Feigin (Ensembl v102 mouse CDS -> GffRead v0.12.7 longest CDS -> PHAST v1.5 msa_view fourfold-degenerate sites -> phyloFit neutral model -> mafSpeciesSubset lineage masking -> phastCons --most-conserved with --expected-length 45, --target-coverage 0.30, --rho 0.30 -> phyloP -ACC -LRT with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 10% -> BEDTools merge/subtract/intersect/multiinter); (2) construction of a test dataset of 17,155 conserved elements on mouse chr19 from the public UCSC 60-way vertebrate WGA, with per-element MSAs extracted by UCSC mafFrags and converted to FASTA by the Galaxy AU MAF_To_Fasta tool; (3) the Lift&Add workflow proper - UCSC liftOver (-minMatch 0.5) from mm10 to macEug2/monDom5/sarHar1/canFam3, CGAT bed2gff.py, two rounds of Liftoff (-exclude-partial, -flank 0 then -flank 1) onto 12 new marsupial assemblies, BEDOPS gtf2bed, BEDTools getfasta, UCSC faSplit, and MAFFT --add (--adjustdirectionaccurately --keeplength --localpair); (4) QC by pairwise raw distances with the R ape package (v5.8-1) dist.dna(model='raw'); (5) a RERconverge v0.1.0 relative-evolutionary-rate analysis of thylacine-wolf convergence (estimatePhangornTreeAll with GTR, getAllResiduals, foreground2tree(clade='terminal'), correlateWithBinaryPhenotype(min.pos=20)); and (6) plots and statistics in R v4.2.1. No wet-lab step is reported: all inputs are pre-existing alignments and public genome assemblies.
granularity_note: 21 steps derived from the 'Materials and Methods' prose of the bioRxiv v1 JATS, one step per named tool invocation, per guide Step 1 fallback (a Snakefile does exist at code/Lift_and_Add/2.Snakefile but was NOT opened - reading workflow source is Stage 2, so the objective anchor here is prose). The README.md of code/Lift_and_Add was read as landing-page prose and is the source of the versions for Liftoff, MAFFT, Snakemake, R and UpSetR that the paper itself omits, and of the environment.yml claim. Directory listings of the repository were retrieved via the GitLab tree API to establish artifact presence only; no script, Snakefile, config or environment.yml content was read.

steps.label: Retain the longest complete CDS per protein-coding gene from Ensembl mouse CDS (version 102, released 2020) with GffRead (version 0.12.7), parameters -C -Q -K -M

Extract fourfold-degenerate sites from the 61-way whole-genome alignment with the msa_view utility of PHAST (version 1.5); no msa_view command line or parameter set is given, and the 61-way alignment itself was obtained privately from Charlie Feigin rather than from a repository
Estimate the neutral model of evolution from the fourfold-degenerate sites with phyloFit (PHAST version 1.5); no substitution model, tree topology source or optimisation parameter is stated

Mask each target lineage (thylacine, grey wolf, Tasmanian devil, giant panda, tammar wallaby, domestic cat) individually from the 61-way WGA with the UCSC mafSpeciesSubset utility, cited only as the kent repository URL https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent with no version, release or commit

Predict discrete vertebrate conserved elements from each lineage-masked 61-way alignment with phastCons (PHAST version 1.5), --most-conserved, --expected-length 45 bp, --target-coverage 0.30, --rho 0.30 (parameters taken from the UCSC phastCons browser track)
Test conserved elements for lineage-specific acceleration with phyloP (PHAST version 1.5), mode -ACC, method -LRT, followed by a Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR 10%

Merge conserved elements within 10 bp, drop elements shorter than 50 bp and discard elements overlapping RepeatMasker annotations for mouse mm10 (BEDTools version 2.3.1; RepeatMasker annotation cited only as http://www.repeatmasker.org with no release, library version or download date)

Overlap the per-lineage accelerated-region sets with BEDTools intersect or multiinter (version 2.3.1) to produce the shared-acceleration comparisons of Figure 1B and Table 2; which of the two utilities produced which comparison, and with what options, is not stated

Download the public UCSC 60-way vertebrate WGA and its associated neutral model (https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/mm10/multiz60way/), filter out sub-alignments containing fewer than 30 species, and predict conserved elements with phastCons (PHAST version 1.5) --most-conserved; the tool performing the 30-species filter is not named and the phastCons parameters are given only as 'as above'

Build the test dataset: merge elements within 10 bp and subtract with BEDtools (version 2.31.1) --merge/--subtract, filter out elements shorter than 50 bp and those overlapping mouse mm10 RepeatMasker annotations, and label the survivors with mouse chr:start-stop coordinates, yielding 17,155 elements on mouse chromosome 19

Extract a discrete multiple-species alignment (MAF) for each vertebrate conserved element with the UCSC mafFrags utility, cited only as https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent with no version, release or commit and no command line

Convert the MAF output to FASTA with the hosted Galaxy Australia 'MAF to FASTA' tool (https://usegalaxy.org.au/root?tool_id=MAF_To_Fasta1) and split it into one FASTA file per conserved element; no Galaxy tool version, no Galaxy workflow export, no invocation identifier and no local equivalent are given

Map conserved-element coordinates from mouse mm10 to tammar wallaby macEug2, opossum monDom5, Tasmanian devil sarHar1 and dog canFam3 with UCSC liftOver (paper states 'version 1.6.3'), -minMatch 0.5, chain files from https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/mm10/liftOver/; the stated version number is not a UCSC liftOver release and appears to be the Liftoff v1.6.3 version carried over in error

Convert the liftOver BED output to GTF with bed2gff.py from CGAT, cited as the master-branch raw URL https://github.com/CGATOxford/cgat/blob/master/CGAT/scripts/bed2gff.py with no CGAT version, no commit SHA and no parameters

Map conserved elements from the query genome (sarHar1 or macEug2) onto 12 new marsupial assemblies with two rounds of Liftoff (-exclude-partial; round 1 with -flank 0, round 2 on the unmapped remainder with -flank 1), then combine both rounds into one GTF; the paper gives no Liftoff version (README of code/Lift_and_Add states Liftoff v1.6.3) and the full assembly list lives only in Supplementary Table 5
Convert the combined Liftoff GTF to BED with BEDOPS (version 2.4.4.1) gtf2bed; no options stated

Extract nucleotide sequences for all mapped elements from each target genome with BEDTools getfasta, split into one FASTA per element with the UCSC faSplit utility (kent URL only, no version), and produce the per-element species summary table; the BEDTools version is not restated for this call and faSplit carries no version

Add the new marsupial sequences to the original 60-way per-element alignments with MAFFT --add (scripts 3.mv_files.sh, 4.combine_seqs.sh, 5.mafft_add.sh), parameters --adjustdirectionaccurately, --keeplength, --localpair (L-INS-i); the paper gives no MAFFT version (README of code/Lift_and_Add states MAFFT v7.5)

Quality-control the MAFFT --add output by computing pairwise raw distances between aligned species with dist.dna(model='raw') from the R ape package (version 5.8-1) under R version 4.40 (sic - the README states R v4.4.0 and the plotting section of Methods states R version 4.2.1)

RERconverge (version 0.1.0) analysis of thylacine-wolf convergence: estimatePhangornTreeAll() per-element trees under GTR, consensus tree, getAllResiduals() relative evolutionary rates with sarHar1/macEug2/canFam3 excluded as redundant, foreground2tree(clade='terminal') binary phenotype encoding, correlateWithBinaryPhenotype() with min.pos=20; procedure follows two named RERconverge vignettes cited as master-branch GitHub PDF URLs

All plots and statistical testing (binomial tests, pairwise t-tests, Spearman correlations, UpSet intersections) implemented in R (version 4.2.1); Rmarkdown analysis scripts published at https://gitlab.unimelb.edu.au/igr-lab/thylacine_canid_convergence_reanalysis/-/tree/master/analysis and rendered at the project's GitLab Pages site

headline.static_readiness: 0/21 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI on 16 of 21 computational steps, NI on 5. This is an above-median prose profile with one structural weakness and one cluster of unversioned utilities. The strengths: the Lift&Add workflow itself is a public GitLab repository containing the Snakefile, the five numbered bash scripts, a config YAML and an environment.yml, with a step-by-step README that names inputs, outputs and the exact snakemake invocation; the analysis half is published as workflowr Rmarkdown with a rendered Pages site; and the parameters that matter most (phastCons --expected-length 45 / --target-coverage 0.30 / --rho 0.30, phyloP -ACC -LRT with BH FDR 10%, liftOver -minMatch 0.5, Liftoff -exclude-partial with the -flank 0 then -flank 1 two-round design, MAFFT --adjustdirectionaccurately --keeplength --localpair, RERconverge min.pos=20 and clade='terminal') are stated explicitly in prose. Version stays at 1 on every RI step because Stage 1 credits the conda environment.yml only as a CLAIM. The five NI steps are all version=0: mafSpeciesSubset (C4), mafFrags (C11), faSplit (C17) and bed2gff.py (C14) are cited as bare GitHub repository or master-branch file URLs with no release or commit, and the MAF-to-FASTA conversion (C12) is delegated to a hosted Galaxy Australia tool with no tool version, no workflow export and no invocation id - a service whose behaviour can change under the authors without any record. The single most consequential defect is not scored as NI but caps the data axis at 1 across C2-C8: the 61-way whole-genome alignment that the entire thylacine/wolf re-analysis rests on was 'obtained from Charlie Feigin', i.e. by personal correspondence, with no accession, no deposit and no documented request path, so the first eight steps cannot be re-entered by an independent reader even though every tool and parameter is named. Stage-2 upside is genuine: the repository ships an environment.yml alongside a Snakefile, so a code check could lift the version axis if that file pins channels, the interpreter and a platform - but the README's own tool list already shows unpinned entries (UCSC liftOver and UCSC faSplit are listed with no version at all), so the likely Stage-2 finding is that the environment claim is partial rather than closed. Read the 0/21 symmetrically: it under-claims by construction, because Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency.
headline.coverage: 21 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS 'Materials and Methods' (Re-analysis of thylacine and wolf accelerated elements; Defining a test dataset of vertebrate conserved elements for Lift&Add; Workflow; Mapping conserved elements from mouse to opossum, Tasmanian devil, tammar wallaby; Mapping conserved elements from Tasmanian devil/tammar wallaby to new marsupial genomes with Liftoff; Getting sequences from each target genome; Adding new sequences to multiple species alignments of vertebrate conserved elements with MAFFT; Using RERConverge to correlate evolutionary rate shifts with thylacine-wolf convergence; Plots and statistical analysis). 0 wet-lab steps: the study generates no new sequence data and operates entirely on pre-existing alignments and published genome assemblies. Coverage = 21/21 (100%) of enumerated steps.

gaps.where: C2-C8 (the entire thylacine/wolf acceleration re-analysis: msa_view, phyloFit, mafSpeciesSubset, phastCons, phyloP, BEDTools merge/filter, BEDTools intersect/multiinter)
gaps.missing: The 61-way whole-genome alignment on which the re-analysis depends is described verbatim as 'we obtained the 61-way WGA, referenced to the mouse mm10 genome, from Charlie Feigin [28]'. It is a modified alignment (dog removed; thylacine and grey wolf added) that exists in no repository: no accession, no DOI, no download URL, no deposit statement and no documented request procedure. The public UCSC 60-way alignment is cited, but it is a different object from the one the acceleration results were computed on. Every conserved-element set, every phyloP p-value and every accelerated-region count in Figure 1 and Table 2 is therefore unreachable for an independent reader.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the 61-way MAF (or the thylacine/wolf chains plus the exact multiz/roast commands that produced it) in Zenodo or a comparable archive with a versioned DOI and a checksum, and cite that DOI in Methods instead of a personal-communication attribution.

gaps.where: C4 (mafSpeciesSubset), C11 (mafFrags), C17 (faSplit), C14 (CGAT bed2gff.py), C12 (Galaxy MAF_To_Fasta)
gaps.missing: Five tool invocations carry no version whatsoever. The three UCSC kent utilities are cited only as the repository URL https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent - a moving default branch - with no release, tag or commit SHA. bed2gff.py is cited as a master-branch blob URL in CGATOxford/cgat, again a moving reference. The Galaxy tool is identified by tool_id only. These are exactly the steps that convert between coordinate and sequence formats, so a silent change in any of them alters the element set downstream.
gaps.how_to_close: State the kent utility release (or the commit SHA of the kent tree that was built), pin the CGAT version and the bed2gff.py commit, and report the Galaxy tool version string plus, ideally, an exported Galaxy workflow so the conversion is re-runnable off the hosted server.

gaps.where: C15 (Liftoff), C18 (MAFFT), and the paper-wide software table
gaps.missing: Two of the three tools that define the method - Liftoff and MAFFT - are never versioned in the manuscript. Their versions appear only in the repository README (Liftoff v1.6.3, MAFFT v7.5). A reader of the paper alone cannot pin them, and the README's 'MAFFT v7.5' is itself an incomplete version string (MAFFT releases are of the form 7.505, 7.520).
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table to the manuscript listing the exact version of every tool used, including Liftoff, MAFFT, Snakemake and each R package, and give the full MAFFT patch version rather than 'v7.5'.

gaps.missing: Internally inconsistent or implausible version strings. UCSC liftOver is given as 'version 1.6.3', which is not a UCSC liftOver release number but is exactly the Liftoff version listed in the repository README - the two appear to have been conflated. BEDTools is cited as 'version 2.3.1' in the re-analysis and 'version 2.31.1' in the test-dataset section (and 'v2.3.1' again in the README); 2.3.1 is a 2010-era release while 2.31.1 is from 2023, so at least one of the two is wrong and it is not recoverable from the text which analysis used which. R is given as 'version 4.40' for the ape QC step, 'version 4.2.1' for plots and statistics, and 'R v4.4.0' in the README - three different strings for the interpreter.
gaps.how_to_close: Reconcile the version strings against the environments that were actually used, and state one interpreter version per analysis block (or ship one environment file per block) so that a reader does not have to guess which of three R versions produced a given figure.

gaps.where: C7 and C10 (RepeatMasker filtering of conserved elements)
gaps.missing: Elements overlapping 'RepeatMasker annotations for the mouse mm10 genome' are discarded, with the resource cited only as http://www.repeatmasker.org - a project home page. No RepeatMasker version, no Dfam/Repbase library release, no UCSC rmsk table date and no download date are given. The repeat annotation directly determines which conserved elements survive into the 17,155-element test dataset and into every acceleration count, and it is a resource that grows between releases.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact repeat annotation used (e.g. the UCSC mm10 rmsk table with its download date, or the RepeatMasker version plus Dfam library release) and deposit the resulting filtered BED with a checksum.

gaps.where: C12 (MAF to FASTA conversion and per-element splitting)
gaps.missing: A required format conversion in the middle of the pipeline is externalised to a hosted Galaxy Australia instance (https://usegalaxy.org.au/root?tool_id=MAF_To_Fasta1). The step has no local implementation in the released workflow, no exported Galaxy workflow or invocation identifier, no tool version, and depends on that server remaining available and unchanged. The repository README reproduces the same instruction rather than replacing it with a script, so the published Snakemake workflow has a manual hosted-service gap at Step 0.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace the hosted step with a local script (or a Snakemake rule wrapping a pinned maf2fasta implementation) in code/Lift_and_Add, or at minimum export and deposit the Galaxy workflow with its tool versions and record the invocation id.

gaps.where: C1-C10 (GffRead, PHAST msa_view/phyloFit/phastCons/phyloP, kent masking, BEDTools filtering and intersection, test-dataset construction)
gaps.missing: The paper links code for two things only: the Lift&Add workflow ('The scripts and associated configuration files are available at .../code/Lift_and_Add') and the plotting/statistics layer ('Analysis scripts are available at .../analysis'). No script is linked for the conserved-element and acceleration analysis that produces Figure 1, Table 1 and Table 2 - the phastCons/phyloP/BEDTools chain is described in prose only. The repository does contain further unreferenced directories (code/whole_genome_alignment, code/misc, code/past, code/mapping_workflow_old), but the manuscript points at none of them, so a reader has no sanctioned mapping from any of these to any Methods paragraph.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a scripts directory (or a Snakefile) covering the phastCons/phyloP re-analysis and cite its path in Methods, and either document or remove the unreferenced legacy directories so the reader knows which code produced which figure.

gaps.where: C15 (Liftoff onto 12 new marsupial assemblies) and the assembly-to-species mapping throughout Figure 3 and Table 1
gaps.missing: The 12 target genome assemblies are named in the main text only partially and by assembly alias (mSarHar1.11, mMacEug1, ThyCyn2.0, sarHar1, macEug2, monDom5, canFam3); the full list with, presumably, accessions is deferred to Supplementary Table 5, distributed as a single .xlsx (media-1.xlsx). No GCA/GCF accession appears anywhere in the manuscript body, and no assembly checksums are given. The paper also has no Data Availability section at all - there is no statement anywhere naming where the input genomes or the derived alignments can be obtained.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a Data Availability statement listing the GCA/GCF accession and assembly version for each of the 12 target genomes in the main text, and deposit the derived per-element alignments (the Lift&Add output) under a versioned DOI.

gaps.where: C13-C19 (the released Lift&Add workflow), as documented in code/Lift_and_Add/README.md and config_compiled.yaml
gaps.missing: The workflow is configured through user-supplied absolute paths: the README documents config keys 'genome_path_query', 'target_species_path' (a TSV of per-species genome and index paths) and a path to the input conserved-element BED, and Step 1 is a bash script that creates a directory tree 'in a specified path'. No reference genome or index is fetched by the workflow itself, so every external resource enters as a local path chosen by the user. Note this is the prose-level reading of the README; the Stage-2 env_capture_class (B vs C) for these inputs is deliberately not assigned here.
gaps.how_to_close: Add download rules that fetch each target assembly from a versioned accession, or ship a resources manifest listing accession plus checksum for every path the config expects, so that the path configuration is verifiable rather than free-form.
